hypotheses.justification: meromorphicOrderAt is defined as `if hf : MeromorphicAt f x then ... else 0` (Order.lean line 50; simp lemma meromorphicOrderAt_of_not_meromorphicAt). Without hf₁, split on whether MeromorphicAt f₁ x holds. If it does, use the existing proof. If it does not, f₁ + f₂ is not meromorphic either: otherwise MeromorphicAt.sub (Basic.lean line 178) applied to it and hf₂ would make (f₁ + f₂) - f₂ = f₁ meromorphic. So meromorphicOrderAt f₁ x = 0 and meromorphicOrderAt (f₁+f₂) x = 0, and the goal min 0 (ord f₂) ≤ 0 follows from min_le_left. hf₁ and hf₂ can each be dropped, but not both: with f₁ non-meromorphic and f₂ = (·-x)^(-1) - f₁, both orders are 0 while the sum has order -1.

Symmetric to hf₁. If f₂ is not meromorphic at x, then f₁ + f₂ is not meromorphic either: otherwise (f₁+f₂) - f₁ = f₂ would be, by MeromorphicAt.sub with hf₁. Both orders are then the junk value 0, and min (ord f₁) 0 ≤ 0 holds by min_le_right. Otherwise use the original proof. Only one of hf₁, hf₂ can be removed; removing both makes the statement false (counterexample in the hf₁ entry).
